video_title: Brandon Jennings says he was just BUILT differently than EVERYONE 🤷🏾‍♂️

quotes.speaker: Brandon Jennings
quotes.summary_phrase: Brandon Jennings on his early high school training and work ethic
quotes.excerpt: I was already training there in the 10th grade. I'm training with the greatest athletes in the world.
quotes.quote: By my junior year, my mom had touched like 250k. This is before the NIL deals. I already had a lane and the way I had to go to make it. I was doing plyometrics. I was at Home Depot. The Home Depot center that they have back then, I was already training there in the 10th grade. I'm training with the greatest athletes in the world. Some of these players were the best volleyball players, the best soccer players, the best lacrosse. All these people were going to the Olympics that I'm working with in the 10th grade, and it was a different type of training. By the time 11th, 12th grade, it was a wrap. My body was different, my mindset was different. I was already doing core work.

quotes.speaker: Brandon Jennings
quotes.summary_phrase: Brandon Jennings on his intense high school training regimen
quotes.excerpt: I'm taking cold tubs. I'm doing all this different things to get my body.

text_blocks.speaker: Brandon Jennings
text_blocks.text: The band work and all that stuff that we was doing, I was doing that in the 10th grade. I'm taking cold tubs. I'm doing all this different things to get my body. I'm just like, I don't even know why I'm doing all this, but it was new to me. We got weights, but I'm like, what is all this band work?

text_blocks.speaker: Zach Randolph
text_blocks.text: He literally was too, though. This man, he was tiny but mighty at the same time.

text_blocks.speaker: Tony Allen
text_blocks.text: Yeah, he was already heavy. Most of them wasn't on that level.

quotes.speaker: Brandon Jennings
quotes.summary_phrase: Brandon Jennings on his high school rivalry with Tony Allen
quotes.excerpt: It's just me and Tony Allen. That's the only person I'm looking at in high school.
quotes.quote: After my 10th grade year, 11th grade year, I'm doing this between the legs. It's over. It's just me and Tony Allen. That's the only person I'm looking at in high school.

quotes.speaker: Brandon Jennings
quotes.summary_phrase: Brandon Jennings on his transfer to Oak Hill Academy

text_blocks.speaker: Brandon Jennings
text_blocks.text: Dominguez was making a little bit of noise, but it's kind of falling off. Steve Smith needs a point guard because Ty Lawson was just the point guard there and he was leaving. I met Steve Smith up in Bob Gibbons tournament up in North Carolina with SCA, and I had a crazy coming out summer. Steve Smith picked me up. I was confident in going to Oak Hill because Marcus Williams that went to UConn, he had went there before. Him and his dad Kelly and Rodney Gille, they all set it up for me to help me get there. Once I got to Oak Hill, I didn't even know nothing about waking up at 5:00 in the morning to work out until I met Nolan Smith.

text_blocks.speaker: Tony Allen
text_blocks.text: Shout out to my boy Nolan.

text_blocks.speaker: Brandon Jennings
text_blocks.text: Yeah, Nolan from DC. So, I'm thinking I'm still coming from Cali. I'm working out, but this is a different type of workout. I'm getting up at 5:00 a.m. now. I got to meet Nolan at the gym to get ready for a season that we're playing almost 50 games. He's like, 'Young fella, it's different. You ain't playing for state here. We play for the national championship and that's it. We ain't getting no state championship from Virginia. Now, we playing for the national title. If we lose one game, it's a wrap.'

quotes.speaker: Brandon Jennings
quotes.summary_phrase: Brandon Jennings on the legends at Oak Hill Academy
quotes.excerpt: The greatest thing was being able to look on that wall and see all them legends.
quotes.quote: The greatest thing was being able to look on that wall and see all them legends up there. The Ty Lawsons, the Rondos, the Stephen Jacksons, the Carmelo Anthonys, the KDs, the Rod Stricklands, the Steve Blakes. I could just keep going. There's so many names and you like, damn, I want to be up there.
